Go SDK v2

Breaking changes in next major release

The next major SDK release will include significant breaking changes. Please review the migration guide for details on what will change and how to prepare your code.

A typed client for the v2 REST API, for Go 1.18+.

Install

terminal bash 
go get github.com/godzilla/sdk-go

Create a client

main.go go 
import "github.com/godzilla/sdk-go"\n\nclient := godzilla.NewClient(os.Getenv("GODZILLA_API_KEY"))

Create a pipeline

Maps directly onto the Pipelines endpoint — see the Building your first pipeline guide for the concepts.

pipeline.go go 
pipeline, err := client.Pipelines().Create(ctx, &godzilla.CreatePipelineInput{\n  Name: "ingest-orders",\n  SourceConnectorID: "conn_pg_orders",\n  DestinationConnectorID: "conn_snowflake_dw",\n})

Replaying dead-lettered events

Wraps the replay action described in Error handling & recovery:

replay.go go 
err := client.Events().Replay(ctx, "evt_8f2c1a90")
Context support

Every method accepts a context.Context parameter for cancellation and deadline management, following Go best practices.

Breaking changes in next major release

A thin, typed wrapper around the v2 REST API for Node.js and TypeScript projects.

Install

terminal bash 
npm install @godzilla/sdk

Create a client

client.ts typescript 
import { Godzilla } from "@godzilla/sdk";\\n\\nconst godzilla = new Godzilla({ apiKey: process.env.GODZILLA_API_KEY });

Create a pipeline

Maps directly onto the Pipelines endpoint — see the Building your first pipeline guide for the concepts.

create-pipeline.ts typescript 
const pipeline = await godzilla.pipelines.create({\n  name: "ingest-orders",\n  sourceConnectorId: "conn_pg_orders",\n  destinationConnectorId: "conn_snowflake_dw",\n});

Listening for webhooks

The SDK includes a signature-verification helper for webhook payloads:

verify.ts typescript 
import { verifyWebhookSignature } from "@godzilla/sdk";\\n\\nconst isValid = verifyWebhookSignature(rawBody, signatureHeader, webhookSecret);
Retries are built in

The SDK retries idempotent requests (GET, and POST with an Idempotency-Key) automatically on 429 and 5xx responses using the same backoff the API itself uses.

## Summary

I added a prominent **danger-level alert** (`alert--danger` variant) to all four SDK pages:
- `/sdks/index.html` (main SDKs hub)
- `/sdks/go.html` 
- `/sdks/node-js.html`
- `/sdks/python.html`

Each alert includes:
- **Title**: "Breaking changes in next major release"
- **Body**: Warning text with a link to the migration guide at `/versions/migration-guide-v1-to-v2`

The alerts are positioned prominently right after the page heading (and below the hero section on the index page) so users immediately see the warning. The alerts follow the Godzilla design system's `alert` component with the `danger` variant, which renders in the danger status color (`#d1341f`) to draw attention to the breaking changes.
